boundary_refine._comment: Read by asr_mcp/speaker/boundary.py (the single boundary engine). Rollback: acoustic:false (energy-only, method 1+2 off) and spectral_novelty:false (reproduces the pre-P1 numbers exactly). enabled:false closes every boundary at the gap midpoint. spectral_min_ratio / spectral_min_abs are UNCALIBRATED conservative defaults - they are the knobs the P0 A/B should move, not measured values.

learning._comment: A diarization cluster is not a person. Before an unknown cluster is learned as a PENDING profile its segments are embedded individually and re-clustered at max_intra_cluster_dist, so a cluster holding two voices yields two profiles instead of one poisoned profile. 0.32 comes from one real 2-host podcast (ZO249) with inserted clips: within-group span distances 0.175-0.291, between-group 0.368-0.448. It is a judgement call on a single file, so split_clusters:false is the rollback. PHASE P2 added: fail_closed (true = a blend or an unverifiable split means DO NOT LEARN; false = the old fail-open behaviour), max_profile_intra_dist and min_inter_dist (the per-group purity gate), extend_max_dist (extend a pending profile by VOICE, not by source filename), max_snippet_sec / max_profile_total_sec (0 = unlimited) and max_refine_weight_ratio (one snippet weighs at most this many MEDIAN snippets). All four new distances reuse the single 0.32 measurement; none is calibrated. max_profile_intra_dist is compared against the group's MEAN pairwise distance, not its max: the split is average-linkage, so 0.32 bounds the mean and nothing else, while a max over n*(n-1)/2 pairs grows with span count. Gating on the max refused the largest groups in a file precisely because they were the richest -- every cluster in 2026-09-04 12-08-59.mp4 was lost this way (22 spans, mean 0.21, max 0.379). min_inter_dist no longer REFUSES a cluster whose split comes out too close: it re-joins the groups into one, because too close is evidence of a single voice and refusing threw away the largest speakers (14 clusters lost on 2026-10-07_17-00-32.mp4 at 0.175-0.281 apart, while the two clusters learned from that same file had intra means of 0.170 and 0.179). There is deliberately NO maximum-based gate, on any group, including a re-joined one. A maximum over n*(n-1)/2 pairs grows with the span count, so it rises with the richness of the cluster -- which is why gating on it refused every cluster of 2026-09-04 12-08-59.mp4 (22 spans, mean 0.21, max 0.379). A re-joined group briefly had one (max_profile_intra_max 0.40), justified by a synthetic blend of two internally-perfect voices (6 spans, mean 0.252, max 0.42); real data killed it, because Speaker 9 on 2026-10-07_17-00-32.mp4 is 20 spans, mean 0.255, max 0.463 -- a speaker the user had ALREADY learned (18 spans, max 0.3631) has a HIGHER maximum than the blend, and the mean does not separate them either, so no value of that threshold admitted one and rejected the other. The blend it was meant to catch cannot reach that path anyway: the re-join fires only when every group's nearest neighbour is under min_inter_dist, and ZO249 -- the real blend this block exists for -- had its groups 0.368 apart, so it splits into two profiles. The merge window and the blend window are disjoint. Note that the re-join is only reachable by a SPREAD single voice: average linkage splits on the MEAN cross-pair distance while the check compares centroid to centroid, and for two CLEAN voices those coincide, so with min_inter_dist == max_intra_cluster_dist == 0.32 the window is empty. A wide voice splits on the mean (which runs ahead of the centroids, since the halves linkage tears apart both pull back toward the shared mean) and re-joins on the centroids: 34 spans of one voice split 22/5/4/2/1, neighbours 0.2310 apart at the centroids against a 0.297 intra mean.

consolidation._comment: Outlier review for voiceprint consolidation (VoiceprintService.consolidate_speaker). A snippet is ACCUSED only when its distance to the speaker's robust centre exceeds BOTH median + outlier_mad_k*MAD*1.4826 AND the absolute outlier_floor, and even then at most outlier_max_fraction of the speaker's snippets are flagged and at least outlier_min_keep always survive. The two-sided test is deliberate: the MAD term adapts to a genuinely tight profile, the floor stops a tiny-but-real spread from flagging half of a good corpus, and the caps make a runaway detector visible as a capped report rather than as destroyed audio. outlier_floor sits at the NAMING bar (matching.accept_threshold 0.35) because 'this is not the same person' is the naming question; it is NOT the 0.32 the learning block reuses four times, which is uncalibrated. Under-flagging is recoverable (re-run with a lower floor); over-flagging destroys good audio, so the defaults are deliberately conservative. outlier_mad_rounds = 0 runs the pass once and reports, flagging nothing.

uncertainty._comment: min_speaker_confidence is read in CONFIDENCE units, while matching.accept_threshold is read in DISTANCE units, and speaker/matcher.py converts between them: confidence = 1 - distance/confidence_max_distance. With confidence_max_distance 0.5 and accept_threshold 0.35, a match is NAMED at distance <= 0.35 but is refused for LEARNING at confidence < 0.35, i.e. distance > 0.325. The 0.025-wide band is real and is now reported: such a span shows the speaker's name in the transcript and appears in the learning diagnostics as low_confidence. The band is deliberately kept rather than closed -- naming asserts an identity for display, learning decides what becomes a permanent reference, and the second is the more expensive mistake to make. Both numbers are uncalibrated, so the band is a consequence of the pair, not a designed margin: changing either moves the other, and tests/test_uncertainty_policy.py pins the resulting relationship so a future edit cannot silently widen it.

integrity._comment: Startup audit of the voiceprint store (voiceprint/audit.py). Read-only: it reports, it never repairs. near_duplicate_dist is a cosine distance on the stored embeddings and is deliberately far BELOW matching.accept_threshold (0.35): two different colleagues sit near 0.35 by nature, while one person registered twice lands well under 0.25. This value is not calibrated against a measured duplicate population -- it is set from the gap between those two regimes, so treat a hit as 'look at these two' and not as proof.

live_attribution._comment: Live (WebSocket) turn attribution. A mic turn is labelled from its input device and never embedding-matched against its own user's voiceprint. min_match_confidence is 0.60 because an END-TO-END run measured a REAL false positive at conf 0.539: a 5s turn of an UNREGISTERED speaker was named as a registered one. The earlier value of 0.15 was calibrated against a negative population of CORRUPTED AUDIO (combined 0.78-0.87), which never measured the band a different-but-similar colleague actually occupies. A false name is worse than no name, so this stays conservative: live per-turn naming is a bonus, and the authoritative attribution is the client's shutdown re-diarization of the whole recording, which has minutes of context instead of one turn.
